title: Integrating building information modeling (BIM) and LEED system at the conceptual design stage of sustainable buildings
central_proposition: This paper proposes a methodology and an integrated model that combines Building Information Modeling (BIM) with the Canadian green building certification system (LEED) to assist designers in making sustainability-related decisions, calculate LEED points, and estimate associated costs efficiently at the conceptual design stage of sustainable buildings.

concept_definitions.name: BIM (Building Information Modeling)
concept_definitions.definition: BIM tools have the ability to help designers explore different design alternatives at the early stage and to transfer the design information to energy and simulation tools for validation and analysis efficiently and fast.

concept_definitions.name: LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design)
concept_definitions.definition: A recognized rating system for green buildings and homes that outlines six key areas: sustainable sites, water efficiency, energy and atmosphere, material selection, indoor environmental quality, and innovation and design process.

concept_definitions.name: Sustainable Design
concept_definitions.definition: The main objective of sustainable design is to create buildings in sustainable cities that are livable, comfortable and safe, leading to reducing the depletion of critical resources and preventing environmental degradation throughout their life cycle.

argument_structure: The paper argues for the necessity of an integrated tool to optimize material selection and decision-making for sustainable buildings at the early design stage. It then proposes a four-phase methodology for integrating BIM and LEED: designing a relational database for sustainable materials, customizing BIM tools, developing a green building certification module, and calculating associated registration and certification costs. A case study illustrates the model's capabilities.
mechanism_or_causal_logic: The core mechanism is the automation and integration of sustainability data and calculations within a BIM environment. This is achieved through: 1) **Database Linkage:** An external database stores sustainable material properties, LEED credits, and cost information. 2) **Plug-in Development (API Customization):** New plug-ins are developed to link BIM models to this external database, automatically identify potential LEED points for selected materials/components, and calculate registration/certification costs based on project parameters. 3) **Decision Support:** By providing instant feedback on LEED points and costs, the model enables designers to make informed decisions that align with sustainability goals and budget constraints. 4) **Efficiency:** Automating these calculations reduces manual input, increases calculation efficiency, and minimizes documentation effort, addressing a major barrier to green building adoption.

testable_hypotheses_or_predictions: The proposed BIM-LEED integrated model will significantly reduce the time and effort required for designers to identify potential LEED credits and estimate associated costs at the conceptual design stage compared to traditional methods.
Buildings designed using this integrated model will achieve higher LEED certification levels or more cost-effectively meet target certification levels due to early, informed decision-making.
The use of the plug-ins linking BIM to the external database will increase the efficiency and accuracy of LEED point calculations.
Designers using the model will report higher satisfaction with the design process and better understanding of sustainability implications compared to those using traditional methods.
bridge_warrants: The paper connects BIM's capabilities for multi-disciplinary information integration with the requirements of green building certification systems like LEED.
It bridges the gap between BIM's design and simulation functionalities and the specific data requirements for LEED credit assessment and cost estimation.
It leverages the concept of 'early design stage' decision-making to improve overall project performance and quality by integrating sustainability considerations upfront.
methodological_critiques: Existing sustainable design tools are limited by evaluating partial numbers of LEED credits for New Construction projects and are not directly linked to specific credits to determine achievement.
Existing tools for LEED-related decisions may use different data sets and building characteristics, leading to inconsistencies.
Many existing tools to measure sustainable design strategies are not directly accessible from within the BIM model, requiring data export/import.
Current BIM tools lack a material library that helps design professionals determine associated LEED credits and do not allow users to export defined data to an external database.
model_structure: The model is an integrated platform implemented as a plug-in for Autodesk Revit Architecture (BIM tool), structured in four phases: 1) An external relational database stores information on green products, certified materials, LEED parameters, suppliers' data, keynotes, and assembly codes. 2) BIM tool customization involves developing a 3D module within Revit to store newly created families of certified green materials and their keynotes, linked to the external database, including a distance calculator plug-in for 'Regional Materials' credit. 3) A green building certification module, implemented as a sustainability evaluator plug-in, retrieves data from the building model, identifies potential LEED points for components (EA and MR categories), and stores this information in the external database, automating point summation. 4) A registration and certification cost calculator, with its own database, computes project registration and certification costs based on project area, membership status, and selected certification type.
limitations: The model does not include all LEED products, focusing only on LEED-NC and specifically on EA and MR credits.
The model does not incorporate cost analysis for each point depending on materials and systems used, beyond project size and overall cost.
The study focused only on BIM and sustainability from the LEED perspective, analyzing only one LEED rating system (LEED-NC).
The integration of BIM and LEED is feasible with considerable constraints.
The model needs to accommodate the requirements of different team members at various stages of the project delivery process.
